questions.prompt: Which belief about commuting does the author call mistaken?
questions.promptZh: 作者认为哪种通勤看法有误？
options: An unchanged, solitary commute would be better than talking to a fellow commuter.
Every commuter is already talking to someone on every journey.
A new conversation must make the train reach its destination sooner.
Keeping to oneself and talking to a fellow passenger are the same activity.
optionsZh: 不改变车程习惯、独自待着会比同路人交谈更好。
每个通勤者每次都已在交谈。
新交谈必会缩短列车运行时间。
独自待着与同其他乘客交谈是同一活动。
analyses: A mistaken to think 后完整列出被否定的预期：维持原状、独处比交谈好。
B 文中未统计每人原有交谈频率。
C 比较的是感受，并非车速或到达时间。
D 两种体验正被对照，不能合并；作者在此讨论通勤例中的判断，不是保证每次交谈都更好。

vocabulary.meaning: 独自待着；不主动与别人交往
vocabulary.context: 在此说通勤中的社交方式，不是保守秘密。
vocabulary.example: The passengers expected to enjoy keeping to themselves.

questions.evidenceQuote: We are clearly mistaken to think that not making any changes to our commute and keeping to ourselves would be better than talking to a fellow commuter. We think sticking to a routine commute is better than making a new social connection: a clear familiarity bias. We settle on a job candidate or potential mate before exploring enough. We need to overcome this familiarity bias in order to explore the new and unknown.

questions.prompt: What makes the routine-commute preference an example of familiarity bias?
questions.promptZh: 为何偏好惯常通勤体现熟悉偏误？
options: The routine has been proved superior on every possible measure.
The author says people cannot form any new connection.
People regard the familiar routine as better than a new social connection.
A new social connection is defined as repeating exactly the same routine.
optionsZh: 惯常方式在一切指标上已被证明优越。
作者说人无法建立任何新联系。
人把熟悉的惯常方式看得比新社交联系更好。
新联系被定义为原样重复惯例。
analyses: A we think 是人的判断，不是所有指标的客观证明。
B 本句讨论偏好，不是能力缺失。
C routine commute 与 new social connection 对照，冒号后的标签解释这种偏向。
D 新联系与守旧被分列，并非同义。

vocabulary.meaning: 坚持；继续沿用
vocabulary.context: 这里指延续惯常车程方式，不是粘在物体上。
vocabulary.example: Sticking to the routine felt safer than meeting someone new.

questions.evidenceQuote: We are clearly mistaken to think that not making any changes to our commute and keeping to ourselves would be better than talking to a fellow commuter. We think sticking to a routine commute is better than making a new social connection: a clear familiarity bias. We settle on a job candidate or potential mate before exploring enough. We need to overcome this familiarity bias in order to explore the new and unknown.

questions.prompt: What is the criticism of settling on a job candidate or potential mate?
questions.promptZh: 对选定工作候选人或潜在伴侣，作者批评的是什么？
options: The choice is necessarily made only after every possibility is examined.
People may settle on someone before they have explored enough.
Exploration is said to make every possible match unsuitable.
The sentence specifies an exact number of candidates everyone must meet.
optionsZh: 选择必定是在查遍一切可能之后作出的。
人可能在探索尚不足时就选定某人。
探索被说成会让所有人选都不合适。
句子规定每人必须见的候选人确切数目。
analyses: A before exploring enough 恰是相反的时间与充分性判断。
B 作者把探索不足时便定下选择列为偏误的表现。
C 没有说探索必毁掉匹配机会。
D enough 未量化成统一人数，也没有把一句概括写成每个人的实际经历。

vocabulary.meaning: 选定；经过考虑后决定采用
vocabulary.context: on 后为选中的对象，区别 settle for 的将就接受之意。
vocabulary.example: They settled on a candidate before considering the full field.

questions.evidenceQuote: We are clearly mistaken to think that not making any changes to our commute and keeping to ourselves would be better than talking to a fellow commuter. We think sticking to a routine commute is better than making a new social connection: a clear familiarity bias. We settle on a job candidate or potential mate before exploring enough. We need to overcome this familiarity bias in order to explore the new and unknown.

questions.prompt: How does the India example support the description of Jobs?
questions.promptZh: 印度例子如何支持本段对 Jobs 的描述？
options: It says he refused to leave every familiar setting.
It places his first exploration of India after retirement.
It identifies familiarity bias as the reason he avoided India.
It presents his eagerness to explore an unknown place at nineteen as a contrast to familiarity bias.
optionsZh: 说他拒绝离开任何熟悉环境。
把首次探索印度放在退休之后。
说熟悉偏误导致他避开印度。
以十九岁渴望探索陌生地方对照熟悉偏误。
analyses: A eager to explore 与拒绝探索相反。
B 明确 at age nineteen，未说退休。
C 书中说 didn’t suffer，并非因此避开。
D 破折号后给出作者如此描述的例子；一次人物事例并非对其一生所有决定的无偏误测量。

vocabulary.meaning: 渴望的；热切想做某事的
vocabulary.context: 形容探索印度的意愿，不表示探索结果必成功。
vocabulary.example: She was eager to explore an unfamiliar culture.

questions.evidenceQuote: Steve Jobs didn’t suffer from a familiarity bias—he was eager to explore the unknown world of India at age nineteen. Unfortunately, he got sick and lost a lot of weight. Yet, years later, he credits his experiences in India for giving him confidence to trust his intuition. He made a lot of brilliant choices and some questionable ones thanks to his unique decision-making style, which balanced rationality and intuition.

questions.prompt: What immediate setback during the India experience is mentioned?
questions.promptZh: 印度经历中提到什么直接挫折？
options: He was unable ever to make another decision.
He became ill and lost considerable weight.
He decided that he had never wanted to visit India.
He immediately gained weight and abandoned all exploration.
optionsZh: 他此后永远无法作决定。
他生病并明显消瘦。
他认定自己从未想去印度。
他立即增重并放弃一切探索。
analyses: A 后文仍谈他的决定，无永久失能之说。
B got sick and lost a lot of weight 明示两个不利结果。
C 不幸遭遇不等于从未有探索意愿。
D 体重变化方向反了，且未交代放弃一切探索。

vocabulary.meaning: 不幸的是；引出不利情况
vocabulary.context: 提示探索也有挫折，与后来归功于这段经历形成转折。
vocabulary.example: Unfortunately, the journey included an unexpected illness.

questions.evidenceQuote: Steve Jobs didn’t suffer from a familiarity bias—he was eager to explore the unknown world of India at age nineteen. Unfortunately, he got sick and lost a lot of weight. Yet, years later, he credits his experiences in India for giving him confidence to trust his intuition. He made a lot of brilliant choices and some questionable ones thanks to his unique decision-making style, which balanced rationality and intuition.

questions.prompt: Which description preserves both sides of Jobs's decision-making outcomes?
questions.promptZh: 哪种描述保留了 Jobs 决策结果的两面？
options: The style produced only questionable choices and no brilliant ones.
Rationality and intuition are presented as mutually exclusive in his style.
The style balanced rationality and intuition and accompanied brilliant as well as questionable choices.
The account proves every intuitive decision is superior to every rational one.
optionsZh: 这种风格只带来可疑选择，没有出色选择。
在他的风格中，理性与直觉被说成互不相容。
该风格平衡理性和直觉，带来出色选择，也有一些可疑选择。
叙述证明每个直觉决定都优于每个理性决定。
analyses: A 漏掉 a lot of brilliant choices。
B balanced 明示兼顾，不能改成排斥。
C both kinds of choices 与 which 从句两部分均准确保留。
D 人物叙述没有比较所有直觉与理性决定，更没有作普遍优劣证明。

vocabulary.meaning: 值得质疑的；是否妥当有疑问的
vocabulary.context: 修饰部分选择，不能误作他提出了许多问题，也不等于全部失败。
vocabulary.example: The unusual approach led to some questionable choices.

questions.evidenceQuote: Steve Jobs didn’t suffer from a familiarity bias—he was eager to explore the unknown world of India at age nineteen. Unfortunately, he got sick and lost a lot of weight. Yet, years later, he credits his experiences in India for giving him confidence to trust his intuition. He made a lot of brilliant choices and some questionable ones thanks to his unique decision-making style, which balanced rationality and intuition.

questions.prompt: What does 'a true one and only' mean in the description of Jobs?
questions.promptZh: 描述 Jobs 的 a true one and only 是什么意思？
options: He was exceptionally distinctive as an individual.
He was the only person ever to visit India.
Every other person would necessarily respond exactly as he did.
He made precisely one decision throughout his career.
optionsZh: 他是极具独特性的个人。
他是史上唯一到过印度的人。
其他每个人必定和他反应完全相同。
他整个职业生涯恰好只作过一个决定。
analyses: A 与 idiosyncratic 同向，强调独特性，为随后推广性问题铺垫。
B 独特是人物特点，不是去印度人数统计。
C 独特性反而引出是否可推广的疑问，非保证人人相同。
D one and only 是固定表达，不是决定数等于一。

vocabulary.meaning: 有独特个性的；与众不同的
vocabulary.context: 形容人物特有风格，不自动含有全对或全错的判断。
vocabulary.example: His idiosyncratic approach raised questions about generalisation.

questions.evidenceQuote: Steve Jobs was idiosyncratic, a true one and only. Is there anything generalizable from his experience in India? Or is it specific only to him? Social psychologists Angela Ka-yee Leung, William Maddux, Adam Galinsky, and Chi-yue Chiu have amassed evidence showing that multicultural experiences seem to increase creativity.

questions.prompt: What possibility does the follow-up question about specificity raise?
questions.promptZh: Or is it specific only to him? 提出什么可能？
options: Every multicultural experience has already been shown to have identical effects.
Jobs's experience is irrelevant because he never travelled abroad.
The researchers have refused to collect any further evidence.
The lesson from Jobs's experience might apply only to him rather than be generalisable.
optionsZh: 每种多文化经历已被证明效果完全相同。
Jobs 从未出国，所以他的经历无关。
研究者拒绝再收集证据。
Jobs 经历中的启示可能只适用于他，不能推广。
analyses: A 问句对推广性提出疑问，并非宣告完全相同。
B 前文已明确印度经历。
C 后句反而转向已积累的研究证据。
D Or 承接前一句 generalizable，以只适用于个人构成替代可能；问句不是已得出的否定结论。

vocabulary.meaning: 特有的；限于某对象的
vocabulary.context: specific only to him 指适用范围，而非仅仅叙述足够详细。
vocabulary.example: The benefit might be specific to one person's circumstances.

questions.evidenceQuote: Steve Jobs was idiosyncratic, a true one and only. Is there anything generalizable from his experience in India? Or is it specific only to him? Social psychologists Angela Ka-yee Leung, William Maddux, Adam Galinsky, and Chi-yue Chiu have amassed evidence showing that multicultural experiences seem to increase creativity.

questions.prompt: What were participants asked to do in the example introduced by 'For instance'?
questions.promptZh: For instance 引入的例子要求参与者做什么？
options: Record only the countries they hoped to visit.
Solve the Duncker candle problem.
Construct a complete house using ordinary timber.
Choose a favourite commuting route without a task.
optionsZh: 只记录希望去的国家。
解答 Duncker 蜡烛问题。
用普通木材建整所房子。
不做任务，只选喜爱的通勤路线。
analyses: A 当前句是任务而非旅行意愿问卷。
B were asked to solve 后给任务名称。
C 造房属于下一段作者的文化例子，不是此处实验任务。
D 通勤属于前一小节，不能移作此处研究程序。

vocabulary.meaning: 解决；找出问题的解法
vocabulary.context: 这里是尝试解题的要求，不代表全部参与者都解出。
vocabulary.example: Participants were asked to solve a practical puzzle.

questions.evidenceQuote: For instance, participants were asked to solve the Duncker candle problem. You have a candle, a pack of matches, and a box of tacks. Can you attach a candle to a wall so that the candle will burn properly and won’t drip wax on the table or floor? (The answer is in the endnotes.)

questions.prompt: Which set of materials is provided for the candle problem?
questions.promptZh: 蜡烛问题提供哪组材料？
options: A candle, a wall hook, and a ready-made candle holder.
A bookcase, timber, and a box of nails.
A candle, a pack of matches, and a box of tacks.
A candle, a pack of tacks, and a box of matches.
optionsZh: 蜡烛、墙钩和现成烛台。
书柜、木材和一盒钉子。
蜡烛、一包火柴和一盒图钉。
蜡烛、一包图钉和一盒火柴。
analyses: A 增加了未给的墙钩与烛台，改变任务。
B 混入后来 DIY 房屋例子的材料。
C 三个物品及 pack/box 的搭配逐项对应原句。
D 交换 matches 与 tacks 对应的容器；细节题需核对完整名词组。

vocabulary.meaning: 图钉；短而头部较大的小钉子
vocabulary.context: 此处是材料清单的一项，不是航行路线或应对方式。
vocabulary.example: The box of tacks was one of the puzzle's materials.

questions.evidenceQuote: For instance, participants were asked to solve the Duncker candle problem. You have a candle, a pack of matches, and a box of tacks. Can you attach a candle to a wall so that the candle will burn properly and won’t drip wax on the table or floor? (The answer is in the endnotes.)

questions.prompt: What is the function of the parenthetical note about the endnotes?
questions.promptZh: 有关 endnotes 的括号说明起什么作用？
options: It directs readers to where the candle problem's answer can be found.
It states that every participant has solved the task correctly.
It supplies the complete solution in the current sentence.
It says the answer is absent from the book.
optionsZh: 指出读者可在何处找到蜡烛问题答案。
宣称每位参与者均已正确解题。
在当前句给出完整解法。
说本书没有答案。
analyses: A in the endnotes 是答案位置提示。
B 指出答案位置不等于统计解题成功率。
C 本句只有指向信息，未展开解法。
D 与 is in 的肯定表达相反；不把这个书内提示当作当前英文阅读题的答案。

vocabulary.meaning: 尾注；书末集中列出的注释
vocabulary.context: 本句把读者引向书末，并非本段脚下的脚注。
vocabulary.example: The reader was directed to the endnotes for the solution.

questions.evidenceQuote: For instance, participants were asked to solve the Duncker candle problem. You have a candle, a pack of matches, and a box of tacks. Can you attach a candle to a wall so that the candle will burn properly and won’t drip wax on the table or floor? (The answer is in the endnotes.)

questions.prompt: What purpose is the candle task widely used for, according to the passage?
questions.promptZh: 按原文，蜡烛任务被广泛用于什么目的？
options: Checking whether all participants have travelled to India.
Measuring only a person's ability to remember train times.
Testing whether every person can build a house.
Testing creativity.
optionsZh: 查验所有参与者是否去过印度。
仅测记忆列车时刻的能力。
检验每人能否造房。
测试创造力。
analyses: A 旅游经历与题目表现可被比较，但任务目的不是查出入境。
B 未提列车时刻记忆。
C 把后续文化例子误移到当前任务。
D for testing creativity 明确给用途；广泛采用不表示单个任务穷尽创造力全部方面。

vocabulary.meaning: 广泛使用的；被许多人采用的
vocabulary.context: 描述任务使用范围，不是保证任何人都会解题。
vocabulary.example: The exercise is widely used as a creativity task.

questions.evidenceQuote: This is a widely used task for testing creativity. Among MBA students, those with more experience living abroad were more likely to solve the Duncker candle problem than those with less foreign experience. These findings were also replicated using different types of creativity tasks.

questions.prompt: What does the replication sentence add to the candle-task findings?
questions.promptZh: 复现结果的句子为蜡烛任务发现补充什么？
options: The findings appeared only when exactly the same candle task was repeated.
The findings were reproduced using other kinds of creativity tasks too.
Every participant became equally creative after moving abroad.
No creativity task other than the candle problem was used.
optionsZh: 发现只在完全重复同一蜡烛任务时出现。
使用其他种类创造力任务，也复现了这些发现。
每个参与者出国后都变得同样有创造力。
除蜡烛问题外，未使用其他创造力任务。
analyses: A different types 恰说明不限于同一任务。
B also replicated 扩大到不同任务的复现，但没有说每人结果一致。
C 前文是海外经历与解题表现的关系，不能补成人人出国后的统一因果变化。
D 与 different types of creativity tasks 明示相反。

vocabulary.meaning: 复现；用研究再次得到相似发现
vocabulary.context: 不是抄写试题，也不是声称一次结果已被全部可能任务证明。
vocabulary.example: The pattern was replicated with a different creativity task.

questions.evidenceQuote: This is a widely used task for testing creativity. Among MBA students, those with more experience living abroad were more likely to solve the Duncker candle problem than those with less foreign experience. These findings were also replicated using different types of creativity tasks.

questions.prompt: What does the opening 'why' question ask the paragraph to explain?
questions.promptZh: 段首 why 问句要下文解释什么？
options: Whether the author ever travelled outside Japan.
Why every person abroad necessarily becomes a professional builder.
How to solve the candle problem using only the information in this sentence.
Why multicultural experiences might be linked with creativity.
optionsZh: 作者是否曾离开日本。
为何每个出国者都必成专业建筑工。
如何仅凭当前句解开蜡烛问题。
多文化经历为何可能与创造力相联系。
analyses: A 下文个人例子辅助解释，并非段首所问的经历核验。
B 从关联到人人必成建筑工，范围和结果都被扩大。
C 问的是关系解释，非蜡烛操作解法。
D associated with 标出关联，后句 speculate 再给一种解释设想；问句本身不证明因果机制。

vocabulary.meaning: 与……相关联
vocabulary.context: 此处保持相关措辞，后续解释仍由 speculate 限定。
vocabulary.example: The researchers asked why the experience was associated with creativity.

questions.evidenceQuote: So, why should multicultural experiences be associated with creativity? Leung and colleagues speculate that people acquire novel ideas and concepts from multicultural experiences. One new concept I learned about when I moved to the U.S. was the possibility of building or renovating your own house. For an American reader, this is an ordinary idea.

questions.prompt: What new possibility did the author learn about after moving to the U.S.?
questions.promptZh: 搬到美国后，作者了解到什么新的可能？
options: Building or renovating one's own house.
The fact that no house can ever be renovated.
A requirement that every resident hire the same builder.
The claim that shelves are unknown in Japan.
optionsZh: 自己建造或翻新房屋。
任何房屋都绝不能翻新这一事实。
每位居民都必须雇同一建筑工的规定。
日本没有架子的说法。
analyses: A possibility of building or renovating your own house 直接对应。
B renovating 与绝不可能翻新相反。
C 自己动手的可能性不是统一雇人的要求。
D 后段反而列架子、书柜作为日本 DIY 例子；不能把作者学到的新概念扩大为两国绝对无例外的事实。

vocabulary.meaning: 翻新；修缮更新
vocabulary.context: 与 building 并列，区分改造已有房屋与新建房屋。
vocabulary.example: She was considering renovating her own house.

questions.evidenceQuote: So, why should multicultural experiences be associated with creativity? Leung and colleagues speculate that people acquire novel ideas and concepts from multicultural experiences. One new concept I learned about when I moved to the U.S. was the possibility of building or renovating your own house. For an American reader, this is an ordinary idea.

questions.prompt: For whom is the idea described as ordinary?
questions.promptZh: 文中对谁而言，这个想法很普通？
options: Only the author's Tokyo college friends, as proved by their recorded replies.
Every reader regardless of cultural background, with no distinction.
An American reader.
The author before he had ever heard of it.
optionsZh: 仅限作者的东京大学朋友，且有实际回复证明。
不分文化背景的所有读者，毫无区别。
美国读者。
从未听过这个想法之前的作者。
analyses: A 此处未给朋友实际回复，其假设反应在后面。
B For an American reader 限定视角，不能删除。
C ordinary 的判断被放在美国读者视角。
D 作者前句把它称为自己学到的新概念，下一段还强调其新颖。

vocabulary.meaning: 平常的；不特别新奇的
vocabulary.context: 本句明确限定看待想法的文化视角，不表示想法无用。
vocabulary.example: An idea that seems ordinary to one reader may surprise another.

questions.evidenceQuote: So, why should multicultural experiences be associated with creativity? Leung and colleagues speculate that people acquire novel ideas and concepts from multicultural experiences. One new concept I learned about when I moved to the U.S. was the possibility of building or renovating your own house. For an American reader, this is an ordinary idea.

questions.prompt: How does 'To me, it was a radical idea' position the author's response?
questions.promptZh: To me, it was a radical idea 如何描述作者的反应？
options: He says the idea was already familiar to him from childhood.
He regards the idea as a striking departure from his previous expectations.
He reports that Japanese law prohibited all DIY.
He defines radical as a political party's official building policy.
optionsZh: 他说自己自幼已熟悉这个想法。
他认为这个想法显著突破自己原先的预期。
他报告日本法律禁止一切 DIY。
他把 radical 定义为某政党的正式建筑政策。
analyses: A radical 与此前习以为常相反。
B To me 限定个人视角，radical 强调与旧想法差距大；不要求它对每个读者都新。
C 后句 does exist 还承认日本有 DIY，未提禁令。
D 语境是自己翻新或造房的新观念，不是政治归属。

vocabulary.meaning: 突破原有观念的；很不寻常的
vocabulary.context: 此处说作者感受到的新颖程度，非必然危险或政治极端。
vocabulary.example: Building a whole house seemed a radical idea to the newcomer.

questions.evidenceQuote: To me, it was a radical idea. To be clear, DIY does exist in Japan, but it typically involves small projects like building shelves or bookcases. I had never imagined that nonprofessionals would try to renovate or build a whole house by themselves. That aspiration, that frontier spirit, was new to me.

questions.prompt: What qualification does the author make about DIY in Japan?
questions.promptZh: 作者对日本 DIY 作了什么限定说明？
options: It is said not to exist there in any form.
It typically means that every amateur constructs an entire house.
It refers exclusively to buying finished furniture with no work involved.
It exists, but usually involves smaller projects such as shelves or bookcases.
optionsZh: 说它在日本完全不存在。
它通常意味着每位业余者造整所房。
它仅指不动手购买成品家具。
它存在，但通常是架子、书柜等较小项目。
analyses: A does exist 强调确有，不能读成不存在。
B but 后范围是 small projects，非人人造整房。
C building shelves or bookcases 明确包含动手制作。
D 让步确认存在，再以 typically 限定常见规模；没有说绝无较大例外。

vocabulary.meaning: 通常；一般情况下
vocabulary.context: 标示常见倾向，避免把 small projects 改成无例外的唯一范围。
vocabulary.example: DIY typically involved small furniture projects in his account.

questions.evidenceQuote: To me, it was a radical idea. To be clear, DIY does exist in Japan, but it typically involves small projects like building shelves or bookcases. I had never imagined that nonprofessionals would try to renovate or build a whole house by themselves. That aspiration, that frontier spirit, was new to me.

questions.prompt: What is being described as new in 'That aspiration, that frontier spirit'?
questions.promptZh: That aspiration, that frontier spirit 说什么对作者是新的？
options: The ambition for nonprofessionals to renovate or build a whole house themselves.
The discovery that no one had ever built a shelf in Japan.
An actual order from all of his Tokyo friends to build a house.
A promise that an amateur house will always cost nothing.
optionsZh: 非专业人士亲自翻新或建整所房的志向。
发现日本从未有人做过架子。
他所有东京朋友发出的实际造房指令。
业余者造房总是零花费的承诺。
analyses: A That 回指前句 nonprofessionals...whole house...by themselves，frontier spirit 概括这种敢于尝试的志向。
B 原文已列日本架子项目，并非无人做过。
C 没有实际指令或朋友调查。
D 本段不交代免费，更不保证成本为零；不把精神比喻读成地理边境或成本结论。

vocabulary.meaning: 志向；想实现某件事的愿望
vocabulary.context: 这里是自行完成较大建房项目的进取愿望，不是呼吸动作。
vocabulary.example: That aspiration to undertake a larger project surprised him.

questions.evidenceQuote: To me, it was a radical idea. To be clear, DIY does exist in Japan, but it typically involves small projects like building shelves or bookcases. I had never imagined that nonprofessionals would try to renovate or build a whole house by themselves. That aspiration, that frontier spirit, was new to me.

questions.prompt: What benefit does the author attribute to American balloon framing?
questions.promptZh: 作者把什么好处归于 American balloon framing？
options: It makes construction unnecessary because houses already exist.
It makes building a house more difficult for every person.
It makes constructing houses easier.
It is said to be an invention made by the author himself.
optionsZh: 让造房不再必要，因为房子本已存在。
让每个人造房都更难。
让建造房屋更容易。
被说成作者本人的发明。
analyses: A easier 是容易些，并非无需建造。
B 方向与 makes...easier 相反。
C that 从句给出作者赞许这项发明的作用。
D American 不等于由叙述者发明，文中没有作者自认发明者；这里只按书中介绍理解，不增加具体技术规格。

vocabulary.meaning: 建造；搭建
vocabulary.context: 在此指房屋建造，不是构造一个论证。
vocabulary.example: The method made constructing a small house easier.

questions.evidenceQuote: American balloon framing is a genius invention that makes constructing houses easier. These concepts were totally out-of-box thinking to me, but now seem quite normal. I bet my college friends in Tokyo would think I was crazy if I decided to build my own house.

questions.prompt: What is the status of the claim about the author's college friends in Tokyo?
questions.promptZh: 关于东京大学朋友的说法属于哪种状态？
options: It records their actual responses after visiting his completed house.
It is his conjecture about how they would react if he decided to build his own house.
It reports that every friend has already built an identical house.
It is a direct quotation from a survey completed by those friends.
optionsZh: 记录他们参观他已建房后的实际回应。
是作者对自己若决定造房时，他们会如何反应的猜想。
报告每个朋友都已造同款房。
是这些朋友填写的调查中的直接引语。
analyses: A if I decided 仍为假设，非完成建房后的反馈。
B I bet 与 would...if 显示作者预计反应，并非朋友实际报告。
C 句中无朋友造房事实。
D 无调查或朋友引语，不能把叙述者猜测转作实测证据。

vocabulary.meaning: 我敢说；我料想
vocabulary.context: 此处是表达很有把握的推测，不是实际下注记录或确证。
vocabulary.example: I bet my friends would be surprised if I changed careers.

questions.evidenceQuote: American balloon framing is a genius invention that makes constructing houses easier. These concepts were totally out-of-box thinking to me, but now seem quite normal. I bet my college friends in Tokyo would think I was crazy if I decided to build my own house.

questions.prompt: What does the example of a smile illustrate in this paragraph?
questions.promptZh: 微笑例子在本段说明什么？
options: The same behaviour must have exactly the same meaning everywhere.
The author has measured the facial muscles of every reader.
A smile is the only human action that can carry a social meaning.
The same behaviour can be interpreted differently in different cultural settings.
optionsZh: 同一行为在各处必须意义完全相同。
作者测量了每位读者的面部肌肉。
微笑是唯一有社会意义的人的行为。
同一行为在不同文化环境中可被不同解读。
analyses: A 前句 different meanings 指向相反结论。
B 是个人经历的说明例，不是面部肌肉普查。
C good example 不等于唯一可带意义的行为。
D A smile 接上同一行为不同意义的观点，下两句展示礼貌判断的反差；并非宣称每个文化中的所有个人都一致。

vocabulary.meaning: 例子；用于说明前述观点的事例
vocabulary.context: 这里微笑用于说明行为含义可变，不是已经单独证实机制的实验。
vocabulary.example: A greeting can serve as an example of culturally variable meaning.
collocations: A smile is a good example

questions.evidenceQuote: Leung and colleagues also speculate that multicultural experiences teach us to recognize that the same behavior can have different meanings. A smile is a good example. I was raised not to smile in front of people because it could come across as impolite. But when I came to the U.S., everyone told me to smile more because it would be more polite!

questions.prompt: Why had the author been brought up not to smile in front of people?
questions.promptZh: 作者从小为何被教导在人前不要微笑？
options: It could be perceived as impolite.
Everyone had told him that smiling was the only polite behaviour.
He had been taught that smiling was physically impossible.
He had measured every stranger's emotions before learning this rule.
optionsZh: 这可能会显得不礼貌。
所有人都告诉他微笑是唯一礼貌行为。
他被教导微笑在生理上不可能。
学习这一规则前，他测量过每位陌生人的情绪。
analyses: A because it could come across as impolite 明示他接受这种教导的理由，could 保留可能性。
B 把后一美国经历的劝告移到此前成长经历，且增添 only。
C not to 是社会行为教导，不是生理不能。
D 原句没有这种测量程序，也不是对所有陌生人情绪的检验。

vocabulary.meaning: 给人以……印象；被理解为……
vocabulary.context: 此处说社交行为可能如何被感知，不是偶然找到某物。
vocabulary.example: A direct remark can come across as impolite in some settings.
collocations: I was raised not to smile

questions.evidenceQuote: Leung and colleagues also speculate that multicultural experiences teach us to recognize that the same behavior can have different meanings. A smile is a good example. I was raised not to smile in front of people because it could come across as impolite. But when I came to the U.S., everyone told me to smile more because it would be more polite!

questions.prompt: What change in advice did the author encounter in the U.S.?
questions.promptZh: 到美国后，作者遇到的建议有何变化？
options: People told him to smile less for exactly the same reason as before.
No one offered any advice about smiling at all.
People told him to smile more because doing so would be more polite.
He was told that all social behaviour has no possible cultural meaning.
optionsZh: 人们因与先前完全相同的理由叫他少笑。
完全无人就微笑给过建议。
人们叫他多微笑，因为这样会更礼貌。
他被告知一切社会行为都不可能有文化意义。
analyses: A smile more 与少笑方向相反。
B everyone told me 明确写有劝告，不能删去事件。
C But 引出与成长教导相反的建议，同一微笑被连到更礼貌。
D 段落恰讨论文化含义，不是否认所有含义；everyone 是作者回忆中的概括，不能扩成全美每个人均受调查。

vocabulary.meaning: 礼貌的；合乎社交礼节的
vocabulary.context: 此处的礼貌评价与作者此前成长教导形成对照，不是测量得出的全球统一规则。
vocabulary.example: In that setting, a smile was considered polite.

questions.evidenceQuote: Leung and colleagues also speculate that multicultural experiences teach us to recognize that the same behavior can have different meanings. A smile is a good example. I was raised not to smile in front of people because it could come across as impolite. But when I came to the U.S., everyone told me to smile more because it would be more polite!

questions.prompt: What adjustment does the author say he makes when returning to Japan?
questions.promptZh: 作者说自己回日本时会作什么调整？
options: He assumes that every country now expects identical facial behaviour.
He deliberately tries not to smile.
He smiles more without making any conscious adjustment.
He claims he can no longer return because he has forgotten how to smile.
optionsZh: 他认定如今每国都期待同样面部行为。
他刻意试着不微笑。
他不作有意识调整，反而更多微笑。
他声称因忘了怎么微笑而再不能回去。
analyses: A 回去要调整，正说明其自身经历中的情境差别。
B consciously try not to smile 逐项对应有意识、尝试、不微笑。
C consciously 与无意识相反，not to smile 也不是多笑。
D 原句说 when I go back，且是选择调整而非失去能力；这里保留其个人叙述，不把它当对所有日本人的统一要求。

vocabulary.meaning: 有意识地；刻意地
vocabulary.context: 说明行为调整需要主动留意，不表示动作完全自动或毫无意识。
vocabulary.example: He consciously adjusted his greeting when the setting changed.
collocations: when I go back to Japan

questions.evidenceQuote: Now, when I go back to Japan, I have to consciously try not to smile.
